notice: All results were produced by running the QTA6 scientific engine (precomputed, not live). Noise profiles are synthetic game scenarios.

districts.name: Quantum Academy
districts.blurb: Learn what a qubit, a Pauli error, a measurement and fidelity are by running real simulated experiments.

districts.name: Neon Labs
districts.blurb: Spacetime Pauli checks: post-select away shots in which a fault was caught, and learn what that costs.

districts.name: Sunset Bay
districts.blurb: Measurement laboratory: readout calibration, zero-noise extrapolation and a limited shot budget.

districts.name: Quantum Core
districts.blurb: Repetition and surface codes: read syndromes, connect defects, and see when a clean syndrome still fails.

districts.name: Circuit Harbor
districts.blurb: Limited qubits, drifting calibration, Pareto trade-offs and shared budgets.

districts.name: Nexus Central
districts.blurb: Final mission: protect three city systems at once under one shared budget.

missions.title: The First Qubit
missions.story: A street-light qubit flickers. Some of its readings are wrong because a bit-flip (X) error strikes it with unknown probability.
missions.learning_objective: Measure a qubit repeatedly; see that probabilities are estimated from finite samples and need enough shots.
allowed_actions: Choose how many shots to measure (10, 100, 1000, 10000)
Repeat measurements until the budget is gone
success_conditions: Measure P(read 1) with a 95% interval narrower than +/-0.02

replay.seed_policy: fixed scenario seed; strategies may be changed and replayed freely

noise.description: Single-qubit bit-flip channel (probability 0.12) applied by Qiskit Aer.
noise.provenance: synthetic game scenario; not a measured calibration of any device (in particular not IQM)

missions.title: The Invisible Phase
missions.story: A qubit in a superposition is losing its phase (Z error). Does the usual Z-basis readout notice?
missions.learning_objective: A phase error is invisible in the computational basis; measuring in the X basis reveals it.
allowed_actions: Choose the measurement basis (Z or X)
success_conditions: Find a basis whose result differs from the ideal by more than 5 standard errors

replay.seed_policy: fixed scenario seed; strategies may be changed and replayed freely

missions.title: Protect the Message
missions.story: A message is stored in three qubits. Read the syndrome and choose which qubit to flip back - if any.
missions.learning_objective: The three-qubit repetition code corrects any single bit-flip but not phase errors.
allowed_actions: For each damaged message choose a recovery qubit (or none)
success_conditions: Recover the logical state with fidelity 1 for each bit-flip message

replay.seed_policy: fixed scenario seed; strategies may be changed and replayed freely

noise.description: Exact noiseless statevector logic; the only noise is the injected error.
noise.provenance: synthetic game scenario; not a measured calibration of any device (in particular not IQM)

score_breakdown.weights_are: pedagogical game-design choices, not physical constants

explanation.plain: That recovery does not match the error; the logical state is damaged.
explanation.scientific: The repetition code corrects single X errors only; Z errors act as logical Z and are undetected.
explanation.math: Syndrome (Z0Z1, Z1Z2) locates a single X error; a logical Z = Z on any qubit commutes with both checks.

missions.title: Sentinel Deployment
missions.story: A 4-qubit core circuit prepares a protected state. Deploy sentinel qubits that watch it, then discard shots where one fires.
missions.learning_objective: Spacetime Pauli checks detect faults on the wires they monitor; post-selection keeps only quiet shots.
allowed_actions: Select which data qubits carry a sentinel
constraints: At most 3 ancillas, at most 30 extra two-qubit gates
success_conditions: Fidelity beats the unprotected circuit by > 0.005

replay.seed_policy: fixed scenario seed; strategies may be changed and replayed freely

noise.description: Two-qubit gate errors dominate (p2 = 1%).
noise.provenance: synthetic game scenario; not a measured calibration of any device (in particular not IQM)

0|none.label: 0 checks, 0 T

missions.title: The Ancilla Budget
missions.story: Each sentinel costs a qubit and extra gates. How many are worth it?
missions.learning_objective: Detection shows diminishing returns: each extra check adds gates that add faults and removes accepted shots.
success_conditions: Reach fidelity >= 0.95 with the fewest sentinels that achieve it (efficient choice)

replay.seed_policy: fixed scenario seed; strategies may be changed and replayed freely

noise.description: Two-qubit gate errors dominate (p2 = 1%).
noise.provenance: synthetic game scenario; not a measured calibration of any device (in particular not IQM)

missions.title: Hidden Fault
missions.story: One sentinel pattern fired. A single fault hit the circuit - but where? Mark every location that could explain the alarm.
missions.learning_objective: A syndrome is consistent with many fault locations; only locations whose flow anticommutes with the fired checks qualify.
constraints: Diagnosis is evaluated against exact fault injection
success_conditions: Select exactly the candidates consistent with the syndrome (precision and recall = 1)

replay.seed_policy: fixed scenario seed; strategies may be changed and replayed freely

noise.description: Noiseless environment (used for exact fault injection).
noise.provenance: synthetic game scenario; not a measured calibration of any device (in particular not IQM)

missions.title: T-Gate Crisis
missions.story: The core now includes non-Clifford T gates. A T gate on a monitored wire breaks the sentinel that watches it.
missions.learning_objective: T gates commute with Z-type flow but not with X/Y-type flow, so check validity limits where T gates can go.
allowed_actions: Choose T-gate placement: compatible sites or blind sites
success_conditions: Protected fidelity beats the unprotected T-doped circuit by > 0.005

replay.seed_policy: fixed scenario seed; strategies may be changed and replayed freely

noise.description: Two-qubit gate errors dominate (p2 = 1%).
noise.provenance: synthetic game scenario; not a measured calibration of any device (in particular not IQM)

missions.learning_objective: Compose readout mitigation, ZNE and allocation under a fixed shot budget and compare against the Pareto front.
allowed_actions: Choose readout, calibration share, scales, extrapolation, allocation

replay.seed_policy: fixed scenario seed; strategies may be changed and replayed freely

noise.description: Two-qubit gate errors dominate (p2 = 1%).
noise.provenance: synthetic game scenario; not a measured calibration of any device (in particular not IQM)

missions.title: Syndrome Initiation
missions.story: Three data qubits guard one logical qubit. Parity checks tell you where a flip happened.
missions.learning_objective: Syndromes locate single bit flips; a correct recovery restores the logical state exactly.
allowed_actions: Choose the recovery qubit for each damaged codeword
success_conditions: Restore the logical state in every bit-flip case

replay.seed_policy: fixed scenario seed; strategies may be changed and replayed freely

noise.description: Exact noiseless statevector logic; the only noise is the injected error.
noise.provenance: synthetic game scenario; not a measured calibration of any device (in particular not IQM)

score_breakdown.weights_are: pedagogical game-design choices, not physical constants

explanation.plain: The logical state is fully restored.
explanation.scientific: The repetition code corrects single X errors only; Z errors act as logical Z and are undetected.
explanation.math: Syndrome (Z0Z1, Z1Z2) locates a single X error; a logical Z = Z on any qubit commutes with both checks.

missions.title: Surface Code Grid

missions.learning_objective: Data qubits, Z-stabilizers, boundaries: a flip fires the one or two stabilizers that touch it.
success_conditions: Use no more flips than the minimum-weight solution

missions.title: Connect the Defects

missions.learning_objective: Decoding pairs up defects; success means the logical state survives, not that your path matches the injected error.

missions.title: The Logical Trap

success_conditions: Find a correction that clears the syndrome AND preserves the logical state on a hard instance (MWPM fails here)

missions.title: Calibration Drift

missions.title: City-Wide Blackout
missions.story: Three systems fail at once: a core circuit (detection), a sensor lab (mitigation) and a logical memory (correction). One budget, three scientific goals.
missions.learning_objective: Allocate qubits, shots, rounds and credits across detection, mitigation and correction; each task keeps its own metric.
allowed_actions: Choose checks, mitigation strategy and shot budget, code distance

replay.seed_policy: fixed scenario seed; strategies may be changed and replayed freely

noise.description: Gate-dominated profile for the circuit, same for the lab, circuit-level depolarizing for the memory.
noise.provenance: synthetic game scenario; not a measured calibration of any device (in particular not IQM)

glossary.def: A two-level quantum system; its state can be a superposition of 0 and 1.
X flips 0 and 1, Z flips the sign of the 1 component, Y is both. Any single-qubit error can be expanded in Pauli operators.
Overlap between the actual state and the ideal state (1 = perfect). Conditional fidelity is measured only on accepted shots.
An ancilla qubit entangled with a data qubit at several moments; its measurement flags faults the check can see.
Keeping only shots whose syndrome is trivial. It raises fidelity but lowers the acceptance probability (kappa).
A classical-post-processing technique that improves an *estimate* of an observable. It does not repair the quantum state.
Measure at amplified noise levels, then extrapolate to zero noise. Lowers bias, raises variance.
The pattern of stabilizer outcomes that signals where errors may have occurred.
Minimum-weight perfect matching: a decoder pairing defects (or sending them to a boundary) at least total cost.
A residual error that acts on the encoded information although the syndrome is clean.
The size of the smallest undetectable logical error; larger distance needs more qubits.
The candidates that no other candidate beats on every objective.
Fictional game currency used to price actions. Not related to any real quantum-cloud credits.
